title: Orchestrate presubmit checks and dependency curation
author: Diego Chen
release_notes: Adds a staged presubmit orchestrator that sequences lint/test lanes and a dependency curation step; no user-facing changes.
description:
Context and motivation:
We have several recurring pain points in presubmit feedback: (1) noisy parallel CI that spins up heavyweight integration lanes unnecessarily for small changes, (2) dependency bump PRs frequently run the same full graph causing flakiness and long queues, and (3) maintainers have to manually curate dependency updates for packages with security/policy constraints.

This PR implements a lightweight presubmit orchestrator that sequences checks by intent and change scope and introduces a dependency curation gate that annotates and short-circuits irrelevant lanes for dep-only PRs. Goals: reduce CI cost, cut median feedback time for small commits, and centralize policy-aware dep curation.

What changed (high level):
- New orchestrator job: .github/actions/presubmit-orchestrator/action.yml and src/ci/presubmit_orchestrator.py. Orchestrator reads PR metadata, modified paths, and repo intent labels to decide a staged pipeline.
- Staged lanes: lint -> unit-fast -> unit-slow -> integration-smoke -> integration-full. Lanes are gated so earlier pass can skip downstream lanes for small/safe changes.
- Dependency curation step: src/ci/dep_curation.py + a thin YAML config at .github/dep-curation/policy.yml listing allowed groups/versions, and a repo-level package white/blacklist.
- CI workflows: .github/workflows/presubmit.yml updated to call orchestrator; removed several ad-hoc presubmit workflows in favor of the orchestrator.
- Tests + mocks: tests/ci/test_orchestrator.py and tests/ci/test_dep_curation.py with path-filtered cases and fixture PR payloads.
- Docs: docs/ci/presubmit.md and a short rolling FAQ in docs/ci/DEPLOYMENT.md describing migration for integrators.

Checklist (tested locally and in staging):
- [x] Unit tests covering orchestration logic and dep curation rules
- [x] End-to-end smoke run on a dep-only PR (see CI run #12345)
- [x] Backwards compatibility: workflows still accept manual trigger and can be bypassed with [ci skip]
- [x] Docs added for on-call and integrators

Commits (summary):
- a1b2c3: introduce presubmit orchestrator module and action wrapper
- d4e5f6: add dependency curation module and policy YAML
- 0a1b2c: wire orchestrator into presubmit workflow; deprecate legacy workflows
- 3d4e5f: tests and CI fixture updates; add docs
- 6a7b8c: address reviewer feedback (fallback policy, logging, retry semantics)

Files/areas touched (high level):
- .github/actions/presubmit-orchestrator/* (new)
- .github/dep-curation/policy.yml (new)
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (modified)
- src/ci/presubmit_orchestrator.py (new)
- src/ci/dep_curation.py (new)
- tests/ci/* (added)
- docs/ci/* (added/modified)

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ava Murphy (reviewer) - 2026-02-19: "Nice consolidation. A few asks: can the orchestrator produce a deterministic trace of decisions for postmortems? Also add an opt-out for repos that still need the old behavior."
  - Author reply - 2026-02-19: "Added structured decision logging (jsonl) and a PRESUBMIT_MODE env var to allow bypass; updated docs."
- Samir Patel (reviewer) - 2026-02-20: "Dependency curation is valuable, but we should be careful about transitive deps in the monorepo. How are we surfacing policy violations to authors?"
  - Author reply - 2026-02-20: "Dep curation now annotates the PR with the policy hit summary and posts a collapsed comment listing offending packages and recommended versions. CI also fails the curation gate for violations so authors get a red X early."
- Lena Ortiz (security reviewer) - 2026-02-21: "Ensure curation policy doesn't accidentally approve EOL packages. Please add a flag to treat security patches as mandatory bypasses to full testing if only vuln-fix bumps are present."
  - Author reply - 2026-02-21: "Added security_bypass rules in policy.yml and a unit test verifying behavior. We also added an audit log entry for each bypassed test lane."
- Ava Murphy - 2026-02-22: "Left one nit on logs and a comment about retry backoff for remote integration smoke jobs."
  - Author reply - 2026-02-22: "Addressed: reduced verbosity at INFO for happy path and added exponential backoff with max_retries=3 for smoke lane triggers."
- Samir Patel - 2026-02-23: "Approving pending CI stability run and a final smoke run in-prod on a feature branch."
  - Author reply - 2026-02-23: "CI run completed; squashed and prepared for merge."

CI and stability notes:
- First CI run exhibited a flaky failure in the integration-smoke lane due to a network timeout against external test-dataset service. Run rerun resolved the transient failure. (See CI job #67890).
- After adding retry semantics that are now part of this PR, subsequent CI runs are green. Final CI status: pass.
- Performance: small change sets (touching less than 10 files and no src/ changes) now get median presubmit turnaround from ~9m to ~2.5m in internal staging (measured across 300 sampled PRs).

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- This PR is backward compatible: manual triggers and [ci skip] still work. Repos can opt out by setting PRESUBMIT_MODE=legacy in repo secrets.
- Gradual rollout: enable orchestrator by default for the redwood/* packages on 2026-03-01, followed by other repos after 2 weeks of telemetry review.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add a lightweight UI in Console to visualize presubmit traces and lane timings (ENG-4280).
- Integrate vulnerability database feed into dep curation policy for automated severity thresholds.
- Expand path filters to infer intent more accurately using changed-test heuristics.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-02-24 after approvals and passing CI. Changelog: added presubmit orchestrator + dep curation gate; no runtime or API changes.

If you want a quick demo: I can run the presubmit orchestrator locally with the included fixture PRs (tests/ci/fixtures/) and show how lane decisions change when flipping policy flags.

Notes for on-call: the orchestrator emits explicit SLIs: presubmit_decision_latency_seconds and presubmit_skipped_lanes_count; alerts are configured in the observability pack under alerting/presubmit-orchestrator.rules.
